_comment: Seeded defects in this fixture. Each entry names the sweep primitive that must find it and, where the first attempt failed, WHAT THE ORACLE ACTUALLY REQUIRES - because a seeded bug an oracle cannot recognise is indistinguishable from no bug.

seeds.oracle_needs: a driver signature in the body; the bare sqlite message carries none, so the exception CLASS is leaked too (sqlite3.OperationalError: ...)

TRUE must match the untampered control and FALSE must differ. The input sits at the END of the literal (= '{q}') and a row literally named 'a' exists, because 'a' is the seed the primitive injects around
POST JSON {param:{"$ne":...}} and GET bracket syntax username[$ne]=; a GET-only scalar endpoint is unreachable by either
real external-entity resolution - xml.sax with feature_external_ges enabled
__proto__/constructor accepted as ordinary keys by a recursive merge, and the effect reflected back

the probe picks its OWN multipart field name, and confirms by FETCHING THE FILE BACK and reading the served Content-Type - so any field is accepted, the bytes are stored, and /uploads/<name> serves .svg as image/svg+xml from the app origin
the owner's marker (marker-A-9c2f) readable by the second identity, and a response shape that does NOT collide with the soft-404 baseline - hence the deliberately richer object
X-HTTP-Method-Override honoured, turning a GET into a DELETE
a state-changing POST with a cookie-only session and no token
a per-user page marked publicly cacheable, still served under a static-looking suffix

a SERVER-SIDE id (sid) that is not rotated, plus GET /api/me proving the attacker-chosen sid is authenticated afterwards. Flask's signed cookie cannot show this class: its value IS the data, so it changes whenever the data does
POST {"email":...} with a spoofed Host/X-Forwarded-Host reflected into the returned link
a token matched by [?&]token= in the BODY, short and predictable (md5(email)[:12]), and the link built from the request host
a message listener with no origin check writing to innerHTML
a DOM source->sink pair (location.hash -> innerHTML) so the class confirms with a browser and reports NEEDS-BROWSER without one

negative_controls._comment: A HIT on any of these is a false positive and fails test_no_false_positives_on_defended_routes.
